question: Mersenne primes 2ᵖ−1 get rarer as p grows. Do they run out?
answer: Mersenne primes 2ᵖ−1 get rarer as p grows, yet the Lenstra–Pomerance–Wagstaff conjecture predicts infinitely many, fitting the data well. That would mean infinitely many even perfect numbers. But a conjecture is not a proof.
move: Rarer and rarer is not the same as running out.

web.label: A horizontal axis of exponent p with a draggable dot and dots marking Mersenne primes that thin out as p grows. Asks where the count is far to the right and whether the primes run out.
